title: Impersonal and passive se: treaties and organisations

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *se* for general or unknown actors from B1 Unit 6 (*Se busca una persona*, *se buscan personas*, *se trabaja mucho aquí*). The same pattern suits the history of treaties and organisations, where it matters what was done and not who did it.

sections.title: Se with a past verb
rows: a singular noun: *Se fundó la OEA.*
the verb is singular: the OAS was founded
a plural noun: *Se firmaron varios acuerdos.*
the verb is plural: several agreements were signed
no noun: *Se hablaba mucho de la seguridad.*
the verb stays singular: people talked a lot about security

items.spanish: En 1947 se firmó el Tratado de Río.
items.english: In 1947 the Rio Treaty was signed.

items.spanish: En 1948 se fundó en Bogotá la OEA.
items.english: In 1948 the OAS was founded in Bogotá.

items.spanish: En los años cuarenta se firmaron varios acuerdos.
items.english: In the 1940s several agreements were signed.

items.spanish: En Chile se prohibió el Partido Comunista en 1948.
items.english: In Chile the Communist Party was banned in 1948.

items.spanish: Se hablaba mucho de la amenaza del comunismo.
items.english: People talked a lot about the threat of communism.

sections.content: The verb agrees with the noun that follows: *se firmó el tratado*, *se firmaron los tratados*. When there is no noun, use the singular (*se hablaba*). The *se* form leaves out who acted; if you want to name them, use an ordinary verb (*Estados Unidos firmó el tratado*).
